[GAPS]  
- EMG/NCS results — required to identify conduction block (definitive for MMN) or alternative patterns (e.g., diffuse denervation in ALS, demyelination in CIDP).  
- MRI cervical spine — needed to exclude compressive radiculopathy or plexus lesion (e.g., tumor, radiation plexopathy).  
- Serum anti-GM1 IgM antibodies — highly associated with MMN (not listed in ordered studies, but often tested in suspected MMN).  
- CSF protein level — may be elevated in MMN (though usually normal or mildly elevated), and helps distinguish from CIDP (typically >100 mg/dL).  
- CK, B12, TSH, glucose, ESR/CRP, ANA results — all pending; critical to exclude treatable mimics.
